Browse option-chain bundles Deribit venue data → Prediction-market bundles → Option chains 12 Venues Deribit Coverage October 2023 – present Chain-days 6,566 Archive 8.07 TB Price per day €1 Turnover (30d) $1.3B Trades (30d) 435.9K Put/call (turnover) 1.46 What's in the data Every option message type, one schema Tick-by-tick option trades Every print on every strike and expiry — price, size, side and exchange timestamp — at full feed resolution. Order-book depth (L2) Snapshot plus incremental Level-2 updates per contract, so you can rebuild the book of any strike at any moment. Greeks, IV, mark & index The venue mark-price stream — mark price, mark/bid/ask IV, delta/gamma/vega/theta — plus the underlying index price, each as its own message type in the contract file. One schema with spot & perps Same normalized, zstd-compressed format as every crypto venue in the archive — a parser written for Binance reads Deribit option files unchanged. 12 chains All option-chain bundles One row per underlying and settlement type. Each chain page lists its coverage, recent days and the largest contracts of the newest day; days are bought in the shop calendar. Why CryptoStruct Why buy Deribit options data here Four things every page on this site is built on — and the reason the numbers above exist at all. We record everything The complete public feed of each venue as it was published: every Level-2 snapshot and update, every trade with its aggressor side, every quote, funding, mark-price and liquidation event — for every instrument the venue lists, every UTC day since we added the venue. Where a venue offers more than one order-book feed, we take the one with the lowest latency, at the depth that feed carries. Nothing sampled, no on-demand capture. Institutional grade Captured co-located at the venue with the exchange timestamp and our receive timestamp in integer nanoseconds, an event-id chain that makes any gap visible, and one normalized schema across 35+ venues — the same capture our own high-frequency trading engine and enterprise feeds run on. €1 per instrument-day Any instrument-day is €1, series-day bundles start at €1 — no subscription, no minimum order, no tiers to unlock. Credit packs lower the effective price and never expire, and free full-day samples from the major venues let you test first. Self-service for everyone Pick the days in the Data Shop , pay by card as a guest and download immediately — no sales call, no enterprise contract, no KYC. Coding agents buy the same files through the MCP server , and the free Agent Skill teaches them the format. Agents: /llms.txt · MCP server /mcp · every page as markdown via Accept: text/markdown FAQ Crypto options historical data — FAQ What is the put/call ratio across the Deribit chains? 1.46 by USD turnover over the 30 captured days to 2026-11-14 — $773.2M in puts against $529.7M in calls across every strike and expiry of every chain, 22,080 put and 26,353 call contracts traded. Each chain page shows its own ratio per day. What Deribit options historical data can I download? Tick-by-tick trades and Level-2 order-book depth for every call and put of an underlying — all strikes and all expiries — as one option-chain day bundle per UTC day. BTC and ETH inverse (USD-strike) chains plus USDC-settled linear chains for BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and more. Do the files include greeks and implied volatility? Yes — every mark-price update (message type 7) on an option contract carries delta, gamma, vega, theta and the mark, bid and ask implied volatilities; the underlying index price is a separate stream (type 8) in the same file, alongside trades and book depth. Open interest (type 18) is recorded from 26 October 2026 on; earlier days carry none. How big is one option-chain day? Large: a BTC chain day is hundreds of contract files and can exceed 4 GB compressed. Days above 4 GB ship as a resumable tar stream instead of a ZIP; individual contract files are always downloadable one by one. Can I get Deribit options data as CSV or Parquet? Yes — every free sample and every purchased tick day also exports as gzipped CSV or Parquet at no extra cost: trades in both formats, plus top-of-book (BBO) quotes as CSV. Timestamps are integer microseconds UTC and the columns load straight into pandas, polars or DuckDB — see the formats overview . Is there a free sample of Deribit options data? Yes — every chain page offers one free contract file (the most-traded contract of a settled day, with its mark-price, greeks and index streams) as the native tick file, as CSV/Parquet export and as a browser order-book replay, and the downloads page carries a Bitcoin and an Ether option contract next to the spot, perpetual and prediction-market samples. No account is needed. How much does Deribit options historical data cost? €1 per option-chain day bundle — the whole chain of an underlying for one UTC day, every strike and expiry — no subscription, no minimum order; each chain page and the shop show the exact price per day. Buy as a guest, download immediately. Do I need an account or a sales call? No. Pick the chain-days in the Data Shop , pay by card as a guest and download immediately — no subscription, no minimum order, no KYC, no enterprise contract, no sales call. Coding agents buy the same bundles through the MCP server . How is the Deribit options data captured? Co-located at the venue, message by message: every Level-2 update and every trade print carries the exchange timestamp and our receive timestamp in integer nanoseconds, an event-id chain makes any gap visible, and one normalized schema across 35+ venues means a parser written for Binance reads these files unchanged. It is the same capture our own high-frequency trading engine runs on — nothing sampled. Analyze. Connect. Trade. CryptoStruct records the complete feed of 35+ venues — every message, every instrument, every day — co-located and nanosecond-stamped at institutional grade, and sells it self-service from €1 per instrument-day: buy as a guest, download instantly, no sales call.
